geology.coordinate_evidence: Registered coordinates match the NASA-hosted impact database to stated precision; prior verification retained. This is not geological boundary verification.
geology.site_geological_context: UNESCO identifies the Vredefort Dome as the oldest and largest known meteorite impact structure, formed about 2,023 million years ago, and notes shock metamorphism, transformed crystal structures, and shatter cones. NASA describes the exposed regional section as including quartzite, approximately 2.8-billion-year-old Central Rand Group rocks, shallow crustal sedimentary rocks deposited about 2.5–2.1 billion years ago, and 3.1–3.5-billion-year-old granites and remnants of ocean crust along a traverse; this is site/regional context, not an exact assignment to the registered coordinate. IUGS describes the Dome as exposing Archean Kaapvaal craton basement and Neoarchean–Paleoproterozoic Dominion Group, Witwatersrand, Ventersdorp, and Transvaal supergroups, and mentions a schematic geological map, but no accessible point-intersection evidence was obtained.
geology.regional_map_source_located: https://iugs-geoheritage.org/geoheritage_sites/vredefort-dome/ (page includes a schematic geological map of the Vredefort Dome attributed to W.U. Reimold; not intersected with the registered point)
geology.source_geological_map: Council for Geoscience. Geologic map of South Africa, 1:1M. National Science Councils of South Africa.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: Registered coordinates match the NASA-hosted impact database to stated precision; prior verification retained. This is not geological boundary verification.
geology.site_geological_context: At site/region level, NASA describes Sudbury Basin as an ancient, deformed and eroded impact structure whose original crater was thought to be at least 200 km across; the collision fractured crust, produced a melted-rock fill, and enabled mineral-bearing material to infiltrate fractures. The Ontario Geological Survey virtual field-trip record identifies impact-related rocks and features including a melt sheet, sublayer, impact-melt dikes and pseudotachylite, and discusses impact evidence in the footwall and hanging wall. NASA also notes nickel- and copper-rich ore deposits around the basin. These are regional/site context statements, not measurements or an exact lithology assignment at the registered point.

geology.coordinate_evidence: Registered coordinates match the NASA-hosted impact database to stated precision; prior verification retained. This is not geological boundary verification.
geology.site_classification: Impact structure / impact crater (site-level classification; not a point measurement).
geology.site_geological_context: USGS describes a large round lake in Quebec marking the geography of an ancient impact crater. It states that the impact occurred in the Late Triassic and that the resulting crater is about 214 million years old. The present circular Manicouagan Reservoir was created when the Daniel-Johnson Dam united two river systems in 1968. These statements support impact-structure context for the named site, not exact geology at the registered coordinate.
geology.regional_map_source_located: https://osdp-psdo.canada.ca/dp/en/search/metadata/NRCAN-GEOSCAN-1-226330 (official Canadian geological-map metadata record located; the read page did not expose map content or a coordinate intersection)
geology.source_geological_map: Garrity, C.P., and Soller, D.R.,. Database of the Geologic Map of North America: adapted from the map by J.C. Reed, Jr. and others (2005). U.S. Geological Survey Data Series 424 .
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The supplied point is regionally consistent with northern Chile's Atacama Basin/Andean Highlands setting, but the consulted official sources do not provide a gazetteer entry, numeric reference coordinate, or polygon intersect for -23.5, -68.1. NASA describes the Atacama Desert as meeting the Andes foothills; the USGS report identifies the Atacama Basin and the Andean Highlands as regional physiographic settings and maps Salar de Atacama among northern Chile's salars.
geology.site_classification: Regional only: high-altitude basin/plateau setting with volcanic and sedimentary components; not a point-specific lithologic classification.
geology.site_geological_context: The USGS describes the Atacama Basin as a major structural basin filled with Tertiary to Holocene continental sediments, alluvium, saline deposits, and playa sediments, with volcanic rocks including rhyolite ash-flow tuffs on the eastern side. It also describes the Andean Highlands of northern Chile as an undulating plateaulike region with volcanic peaks and internally drained basins. NASA describes salt pans, mineral-streaked sediments, and volcanoes in the Atacama/Andes landscape. These are regional/site-context observations and do not locate the registered point within a specific mapped unit.

regional_map_source_located.description: USGS Professional Paper 811, Geology of Salars, Northern Chile. Includes an index map of salars and regional physiographic maps, plus discussion of the Atacama Basin and Andean Highlands; no coordinate-level map intersection for the registered point was obtained.

geology.source_geological_map: Gómez, J., Schobbenhaus, C. & Montes, N.E., compilers. Geological Map of South America 2018. Scale 1:5 000 000. Commission for the Geological Map of the World (CGMW), Colombian Geological Survey and Geological Survey of Brazil.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The supplied point (-24.6, 15.0; 24°36′S, 15°00′E) is geographically consistent with the broad Namib Desert setting described in the BGR Namibia hydrogeological/geological report. The report describes the Namib as a broad coastal desert zone with rocky desert, sand seas, and stony/rocky plains, and maps Namib Desert surficial sand-and-gravel units regionally. The sources read do not define an exact polygon named "Namib gravel desert" or explicitly locate the supplied point inside one.
geology.site_classification: sedimentary (regional/site context only: unconsolidated to semi-consolidated sand and gravel, locally calcrete, described by the BGR report as Cenozoic Namib Desert surficial sediments; not assigned to the exact point)
geology.site_geological_context: Regional context from the BGR HYMNAM simplified lithological map/report: Unit 2 is unconsolidated to semi-consolidated sand and gravel, locally calcrete, and occurs abundantly in the Namib Desert between Walvis Bay and Oranjemund; it contains Cenozoic sediments of the Namib Desert. The same report notes that Namib landscapes include rocky desert, sand seas, and stony/rocky plains. The IUGS page describes the distinct Namib Sand Sea as Quaternary/Holocene aeolian sand overlying the Neogene Tsondab Sandstone Formation, but that named sand-sea reference is not an exact match for the registered point.

regional_map_source_located.map_evidence: The report's simplified lithological map and accompanying text identify regional Namib Desert Unit 2 as unconsolidated to semi-consolidated sand and gravel, locally calcrete, containing Cenozoic Namib sediments. The consulted text does not provide a point-level map intersection for -24.6, 15.0.

The USGS catalog describes a McMurdo Dry Valleys satellite-image map covering 77°–78° S and 159°20′–163°57′ E; the registered point falls within this published map coverage. This is map coverage evidence, not an exact named-feature boundary.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The registered WGS84 point (64.4, -18.8) falls within the published extent of the Iceland Bedrock Geology Feature Service (west -24.7450703623, south 63.2101412487, east -13.1892454103, north 66.5712584152). This verifies inclusion in the national map extent, not membership in an exact named polygon called Icelandic volcanic highlands. The supplied name is a broad regional descriptor, so no exact feature-boundary match is asserted.
geology.site_classification: volcanic (regional/site-name context only; not an exact-point measurement)
geology.site_geological_context: Regional context only: the Icelandic Institute of Natural History identifies geological maps as covering Icelandic bedrock and tectonics. The referenced Iceland Bedrock Geology map broadly outlines Icelandic bedrock geology, classifies bedrock by age, type, and composition, and depicts volcanic zones and Holocene eruption sites. These sources support a volcanic-highlands regional screening, but they do not by themselves establish the rock unit, age, or mineralogy at the registered coordinate without a point intersection.
geology.source_geological_map: IS-NI contribution to EGDI 1:1 Million pan-european Surface Geology: NI_J600v_berg bedrock and IS 50V Vatnafar water bodies.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The supplied point is identified by the task as the registered WGS84 coordinate for the Amboy volcanic field/Mojave site. The authoritative sources read here describe Amboy Crater and its surrounding volcanic field but do not publish a coordinate pair or a point-in-polygon test for 34.55, -115.78. Therefore the point is not confirmed as an exact crater, cone, lava-flow, or mapped-unit location from these sources alone.
geology.geological_unit: Volcanic flow rocks and minor pyroclastic deposits
geology.site_classification: Volcanic, specifically a basaltic/mafic volcanic-field setting at site or regional level; this is not an exact classification of the registered point.
geology.site_geological_context: USGS Surficial Geologic Map of the Amboy 30' x 60' Quadrangle states that Quaternary volcanic rocks crop out in the southwestern map area and identifies Amboy Crater as a series of basaltic cinder and lava-flow deposits capped by a breached cinder cone. Its mapped unit Qmv is mafic volcanic rocks (Quaternary), chiefly basaltic at Amboy Crater, consisting mainly of cinder cones with subordinate lava flows; the pamphlet reports 79 ka at Amboy Crater from cosmogenic 36Cl dating. BLM independently describes Amboy Crater as ash and cinders, a volcanic cinder cone, and notes basaltic lava covering about 24 square miles with lava lakes, collapsed lava tubes and sinks, spatter cones, and massive basalt flows. These are qualified site/regional facts and do not establish the lithology, unit, age, or minerals at the exact registered coordinate.
geology.source_geological_map: Jennings, C.W., Gutierrez, C., Bryant, W., Saucedo, G., and Wills, C., 2010, Geologic Map of California: California Geological Survey Geologic Data Map GDM-2.2010.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The USGS Mauna Kea volcano page lists Mauna Kea on the Island of Hawai'i at latitude 19.82° N and longitude 155.47° W, which matches the registered WGS84 point to the stated precision. This verifies the point as the USGS reference coordinate for the named Mauna Kea feature, not as an exact boundary or parcel intersection.
geology.geological_unit: Scoria cones of the Older volcanic rocks member of the Laupāhoehoe Volcanics
geology.site_classification: Volcanic, basaltic shield-volcano setting (site-level classification; not an exact point lithology).
geology.site_geological_context: USGS describes Mauna Kea as a shield volcano composed of basalt. Tall summit cinder cones and lava flows underlie its steep upper flanks. The volcano has evolved beyond the shield-building stage, and its most recent eruption is dated by USGS to approximately 6,000-4,000 years ago. The USGS geological-map record describes mapped lava flows, cinder cones, and glacial deposits of the Laupahoehoe Volcanics on Mauna Kea. These statements support site/volcano context only; they do not identify the rock unit or age at the registered point.
geology.regional_map_source_located: USGS, 'Geologic map of Mauna Kea, showing generalized distribution of lava flows, cinder cones, and glacial deposits of the Laupahoehoe Volcanics' (Wolfe et al., 1997): https://www.usgs.gov/media/images/geologic-map-mauna-kea-showing-generalized-distribution-lava
geology.source_geological_map: Sherrod, D.R., Sinton, J.M., Watkins, S.E., and Brunt, K.M., 2021, Geologic map of the State of Hawaiʻi: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Map 3143, pamphlet 72 p., 5 sheets, scales 1:100,000 and 1:250,000, https://doi.org/10.3133/sim3143. https://doi.org/10.3133/sim3143.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

site_level_values.coordinate_status: APPROXIMATE screening coordinate; not a verified polygon centroid or acquisition coordinate

coordinate_evidence: The IUGS Global Geosites Ries Crater page identifies the named feature as Nördlinger Ries, Bavaria/Baden-Württemberg, Germany, and gives a reference coordinate of 48°53′03″N, 010°33′25″E (48.8841667, 10.5569444).

The same IUGS page describes the Ries as a 25 km wide depression. The registered point is approximately 4.634 km from the IUGS reference coordinate, so it is consistent with the broad regional feature on a screening basis.

This is not an exact polygon intersection: the IUGS coordinate is a site reference coordinate and the source text does not establish that the registered point lies on a mapped boundary or a particular mapped unit.

coordinate_evidence: The IUGS Global Geosites Ries Crater page identifies the named feature as Nördlinger Ries, Bavaria/Baden-Württemberg, Germany, and gives a reference coordinate of 48°53′03″N, 010°33′25″E (48.8841667, 10.5569444).

The same IUGS page describes the Ries as a 25 km wide depression. The registered point is approximately 4.634 km from the IUGS reference coordinate, so it is consistent with the broad regional feature on a screening basis.

This is not an exact polygon intersection: the IUGS coordinate is a site reference coordinate and the source text does not establish that the registered point lies on a mapped boundary or a particular mapped unit.
geology.site_classification: complex terrestrial impact crater/impact structure (site-level classification; not a volcanic structure)
geology.site_geological_context: The Ries is a well-preserved, approximately 25–26 km wide Miocene impact structure. IUGS describes a crater floor formed by post-impact Ries-lake sediments with a Pleistocene loess veneer; impact-produced or impact-modified materials include suevite, polymict bunte breccia, polymict crystalline breccia, and crystalline-basement material. NASA reports suevite in Nördlingen’s St. George’s Church and shocked quartz as evidence supporting impact origin. A peer-reviewed Geological Society of America study describes the basin as containing post-impact lacustrine sediments, reworked and graded suevite, melt-rich and melt-poor suevite, and crystalline basement in the Nördlingen 1973 borehole; it dates formation to 14.808 ± 0.021 Ma. These are regional/site or borehole-context observations, not an exact lithology, unit, age, or mineralogical measurement at 48.88, 10.62.
geology.regional_map_source_located: Peer-reviewed Geological Society of America article: Figure 1 is a geological map of the Ries crater with seismic lines; the accessible article text also describes the mapped central basin, inner crystalline ring, suevite, lacustrine sediments, and crystalline basement. https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/geology/article/52/1/39/628384/Understanding-the-Ries-impact-structure-subsurface

original_registry_metadata.source_provenance: Candidate name and approximate planning point proposed in this audit; no site polygon or independent coordinate verification performed. Confirm against official gazetteer/geologic map before acquisition.
original_registry_metadata.notes: Proposed screening point only; verify crater boundary and avoid implying a lunar climate analogue.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The registered point is in the Lonar, Maharashtra regional vicinity, but the authoritative source pages read within the search/read budget did not provide a machine-readable crater polygon or an explicit coordinate that permits a point-in-polygon test. The point is therefore not verified as lying inside the named Lonar impact-crater feature.
geology.rock_type: flood basalt(s); mafic volcanic rocks; basalt
geology.site_classification: site-level impact crater in basaltic target rock; simple crater
geology.site_geological_context: USGS describes Lonar Crater as the only known terrestrial impact crater in basalt and reports shock-metamorphosed material, including coarse breccia, microbreccia, shocked fragments containing maskelynite, melted and vesiculated plagioclase, and glassy impact material. The Geological Society of America mapping study describes a 1.88-km-diameter simple crater formed entirely within the Deccan traps, with mapped basalt flows, impact-related deformation, a continuous ejecta blanket, and glassy impact spherules. These are site-level observations and are not an exact lithologic or mineralogical assignment for the registered point.
geology.regional_map_source_located: The Geological Society of America publication explicitly states that it presents a meter-scale-resolution digital elevation model and a geological map of Lonar Crater and the surrounding area: https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/gsabulletin/article-abstract/122/1-2/109/125471/Geology-of-Lonar-Crater-India
geology.source_geological_map: Chorlton, L.B. Generalized geology of the world: bedrock domains and major faults in GIS format: a small-scale world geology map with an extended geological attribute database. doi: 10.4095/223767. Geological Survey of Canada, Open File 5529.
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

coordinate_verification_evidence.coordinate_verification_status: site identity supported; exact coordinate-to-feature match not verified
coordinate_verification_evidence.coordinate_evidence: The requested point is associated by the project registration with Wolfe Creek impact structure. NASA's official Earth Observatory page describes Wolfe Creek Crater in Western Australia, and the USGS publication explicitly includes detailed geological maps and cross-sections for Wolfe Creek Meteorite Crater. Geoscience Australia's official metadata identifies a GSWA Wolfe Creek Crater elevation grid with approximately 0.0001-degree (~11 m) cells. None of the three read source pages exposed a crater boundary polygon or an explicit reference latitude/longitude for direct point comparison, so the supplied WGS84 point cannot be confirmed as the exact crater center or interior polygon.

geology.coordinate_verification_status: site identity supported; exact coordinate-to-feature match not verified
geology.coordinate_evidence: The requested point is associated by the project registration with Wolfe Creek impact structure. NASA's official Earth Observatory page describes Wolfe Creek Crater in Western Australia, and the USGS publication explicitly includes detailed geological maps and cross-sections for Wolfe Creek Meteorite Crater. Geoscience Australia's official metadata identifies a GSWA Wolfe Creek Crater elevation grid with approximately 0.0001-degree (~11 m) cells. None of the three read source pages exposed a crater boundary polygon or an explicit reference latitude/longitude for direct point comparison, so the supplied WGS84 point cannot be confirmed as the exact crater center or interior polygon.
geology.rock_type: Dunes, sandplain with dunes and swales; may include numerous interdune claypans; may be locally gypsiferous
geology.site_classification: meteorite impact crater / impact structure; USGS describes Wolfe Creek Meteorite Crater as a classic bowl-shaped Barringer-type crater
geology.site_geological_context: NASA reports an approximately 880 m diameter, well-preserved crater with a mostly flat floor, a central rise, gypsum in the center, and iron-shale balls derived partly from the meteorite and impact-modified terrestrial rocks; NASA reports an estimated formation age of about 300,000 years. The USGS publication reports well-bedded ejecta units, crater-floor faults and sinkholes, a ringed aeromagnetic anomaly, rim-skirting dunes, and numerous iron-rich shale balls. These are site-level descriptions and do not establish the lithology, geological unit, age, or mineralogy at the supplied point.
geology.regional_map_source_located: USGS, Geology of five small Australian impact craters: https://www.usgs.gov/publications/geology-five-small-australian-impact-craters (official publication page states that detailed geological maps and cross-sections include Wolfe Creek). Geoscience Australia, GSWA Wolfe Creek Crater Elevation Grid Geodetic: https://ecat.ga.gov.au/geonetwork/srv/api/records/f2e66cab-8acf-4c10-ae9c-6f2da8f9d1a6?language=eng (official geodetic elevation grid metadata; not a lithological map).
geology.source_geological_map: Raymond, O.L., Liu, S., Gallagher, R., Zhang, W., Highet, L.M. Surface Geology of Australia 1:1 million scale dataset 2012 edition. Commonwealth of Australia (Geoscience Australia).
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.

geology.coordinate_evidence: The supplied WGS84 point (-22, 118) is treated only as a screening point for the broad Pilbara rocky-uplands region. The reviewed authoritative sources document Pilbara-wide mapping and regional geology, but do not provide a gazetteer entry or polygon intersect proving that this exact point is a named feature or an exact rocky-uplands polygon.
geology.rock_type: Dolomite, calcareous dolomite, calcrete; with silcrete, clay, chert breccia, and local basal conglomerate.
geology.site_classification: Regional Pilbara rocky-upland screening context only; the Pilbara is documented as an exposed Archean cratonic terrain containing granite-greenstone terranes and younger basin rocks, but the exact point's volcanic, sedimentary, igneous, or impact class is unverified.
geology.site_geological_context: Geoscience Australia describes the Pilbara craton as a mid-Archean province with rocks spanning approximately 3.65-2.8 Ga, and notes extensive exposure near the approximately 2765 Ma Hamersley Basin unconformity. The same project used regional 1:100,000 and thematic 1:500,000 geological mapping, GIS synthesis, geophysics, petrology, geochemistry, and isotopic age data. This supports regional geological context only and does not identify the unit at -22, 118.
geology.regional_map_source_located: Official Geological Survey of Western Australia mapping catalogue/page: statewide geological maps and digital spatial layers are available from 1:100,000 to 1:10,000,000, including GeoVIEW.WA/DASC products. Geoscience Australia’s North Pilbara Project page documents 1:100,000 geological mapping, a 1:1.5M atlas, and 1:500,000 thematic maps, but no coordinate-intersected map result was obtained in this time-limited check.
geology.source_geological_map: Raymond, O.L., Liu, S., Gallagher, R., Zhang, W., Highet, L.M. Surface Geology of Australia 1:1 million scale dataset 2012 edition. Commonwealth of Australia (Geoscience Australia).
geology.evidence_class: Primary geological map interpretation aggregated by Macrostrat v2, with independent local point-in-polygon check; not rock assay or exact site survey
geology.geology_provider: Macrostrat API v2; original map citation retained
geology.missing_reason: Mineralogy always null: no analytical mineral measurements. Exact rock/unit/age null unless a returned map geometry covers the point; coarse map assignment is not local geological ground truth.
